context_requirements: Cells must express PP1/PP2A holoenzymes and have intact phosphorylation-dependent signaling.
Response is expected in most proliferating human cell lines; hepatocyte-like lines may show stronger stress and metabolic responses.
TP53 status may modulate the balance between cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis but is not required for the primary transcriptional response.
falsifiers: No consistent change in phosphorylation-responsive immediate early genes (EGR1, FOS, JUN) at 6 h across responsive lines.
No decrease in proliferation-associated genes (e.g., CCND1, MYC, CCNA2, BIRC5) at 24 h.
No evidence of cell-cycle arrest or apoptosis at 24 h in any of the nine lines.
A response pattern indistinguishable from vehicle across all lines and time points.

evidence.supports: Okadaic acid, a PP1/PP2A inhibitor, induces apoptosis-like morphological changes in MCF-7 and other mammalian cells within hours.
Prolonged exposure to the PP1/PP2A inhibitor microcystin-LR causes dose-dependent hepatotoxicity and enzyme changes in rats.
Okadaic acid inhibits PP1/PP2A and causes cell-cycle and cytokinesis defects in Trypanosoma brucei.
